A “Setu” coin with a bull on the obverse: “Setu” sika bi a nantwinini bi wɔ n’anim. Asɛmfua Setu — abɔntenban a ɛkɔ Lanka, wɔ Rameswaram — pue wɔ mfinimfini mmere mu Tamil sodifo a na wɔwɔ Jaffna ahemman no mu no sika so; nantwinini a ɔda so, Shiva’s Nandi, ne wɔn mfiri a wɔtaa de di dwuma.
A burial urn of the kind that made Adich: Amusiei ahina a ɛte sɛ nea ɛmaa Adichanallur gyee din. Wɔde awufoɔ — anaa wɔn nnompe a wɔaboaboa ano — guu nkukuo a ɛte saa a wɔde adamoa nneɛma gu mu na wɔsiee wɔn wɔ asase a abotan ayɛ so wɔ Thamirabarani atifi. Nkukuo no yɛ abusuabɔ tẽẽ a ɛda Sangam anwensɛm mu முதுமக்கள் தாழி .
A catalogue of the coins issued by the C: Sika a Chera, Chola, ne Pandya ahemfo de mae no din a wɔahyehyɛ, a wɔn adehye agyiraehyɛde ahorow a ɛkyerɛ agyan, ɔsebɔ, ne mpataa ka ho.
A ceramic vessel from Adichanallur. Smal: Nkuku a wɔde dɔte ayɛ a efi Adichanallur. Wɔde nkuku nketewa te sɛ eyi guu amusiei nkuku no mu anaa nkyɛn, ebia na wɔde aduan, nsu anaa afɔrebɔ ma awufo — Dade Mmere mu gyidi a ɛfa akwantu a ɛboro owu so ho mfonini ketewaa bi.
A chariot for a creeper, a shawl for a p: Teaseɛnam ma ɔkraman a ɔwea, shawl ma akokɔ, aduaba a ɛma nkwa ma anwensɛm kyerɛwfo: akyɛde a agye din sen biara a wɔn a wɔba hɔ no de ma no te sɛ nea mfaso nni so, na ɛno ne wɔn asɛm. Kodai madam yɛ ayamye a ɛdɔɔso araa ma nea ɔde ma no mmu akyɛde no a wɔde bedi dwuma no ho akontaa — ayamhyehye a ɛtrɛw kɔɔ mmoa, afifide ne adesua nyinaa so.
A Chera coin in the collection of the Na: Chera sika bi a ɛwɔ Napier Tete Nneɛma Akorae, Thiruvananthapuram, nneɛma a wɔaboaboa ano. Chera sika no su da agyan ne agyan, ahemman no agyiraehyɛde, na mfitiase nhwɛso pii fi Karur, Cherafo mfinimfini wɔ Amaravathifo so.
A chieftain of the Ay line in the southe: Ay abusua no mu panyin bi a ɔwɔ Podiyil (Pothigai) nkoko so anafo fam. Atetesɛm bi a wonim no yiye ka sɛnea ɔde atade a ɛsom bo ma onyame bi, a wɔtaa frɛ no Shiva — ɔma sɛ ahofama ne ayamye nso ho asɛm.
A chieftain of the Malaiyaman lineage, o: Malaiyaman abusua mu panyin bi, a ofi ɔman a atwa Mullur ne Tirukkoyilur ho ahyia no mu, kaee n’adɔe a ɔde maa anwensɛm akyerɛwfo ne wɔn a wɔbaa ne nkyɛn nyinaa. Ne gyinabea wɔ nnipa baason a wɔboa no no mu no kyerɛ sɛ na wɔde ntoboa a ɔde mae te sɛ nea wɔde n’asasesin susuw sodifo nidi.
A Chola coin carrying Pandya royal insig: Chola sika bi a Pandya adehye agyiraehyɛde wom. Bere a Cholafo de Pandya man no baa wɔn nniso ase no, wɔde Pandya mpataa no too wɔn ankasa ɔsebɔ nkyɛn — nkonimdi ho sɛnkyerɛnne a wɔde bɔɔ dade.
A city where literature, royal patronage: Kurow a nhoma, adehye mmoa, nyamesom ne nkurow akɛse mu asetra ahyiam bɛyɛ mfe mpem abien ni.
A coin of Kulottunga Chola bearing the t: Kulottunga Chola sika bi a wɔakyerɛw so sɛ “Malai Nadu konda Chola” — Cholafo a wɔfaa nkoko so man no, kyerɛ sɛ, Chera asase no. Chola ahemfo de abodin ahorow a wɔde abɔ wɔn sika so ne nea wɔasen wɔ wɔn nkyerɛwee mu nso bɔɔ wɔn nkonimdi ho dawuru.
A coin of Kulottunga I (1070–1120 CE), w: Kulottunga I (1070–1120 Y.B.), a ɔkaa Cholafo ne Apuei Fam Chalukya abusua no boom na odii Cholafo ahenni a ɛware na edi yiye sen biara no biako so no sika. Ne sika no toa Chola ahorow a wɔde asi hɔ no so a ne din wɔ Nagari kasa mu.
A coin of Rajaraja I. His copper coins o: Rajaraja I sika bi.Ne kɔbere sika a ɛte sɛ ɔhene a ogyina hɔ ne nea ɔte ase a ɔde bae bere a odii Sri Lanka atifi fam nkonim akyi no dii akɔneaba kɛse wɔ po no afanu nyinaa na wosuasuaa no mfehaha pii.
A coin of the Jaffna kingdom showing a h: Jaffna ahemman no sika bi a ɛkyerɛ ɔpɔnkɔ bi a okura mpataa. Tamil ahemfo a wɔwɔ Jaffna (afeha a ɛto so 13–17) de sika mae wɔ South India atetesɛm bi mu, na ɛyɛ nkaebɔ a ɛfa abusuabɔ a emu yɛ den a ɛda Palk Strait no ntam no ho.
A coin of the Kongu Cheras, the Chera li: Kongu Cheras sika bi, Chera abusua a edii Kongu man a ɛwɔ Tamil mantam atɔe fam (a ɛbɛn nnɛyi Coimbatore, Erode ne Karur ho) — ɔmantam koro no ara a ama wɔanya Roma sika a wɔaboaboa ano a ɛyɛ fɛ.
A Crowned Figure: Mfonini a Wɔde Abotiri Ahyɛ So
A crowned, moustached figure in profile,: Ɔbarima bi a ɔhyɛ abotiri a ne abɔgyesɛ wɔ ne ho so, a ɔhyɛ jacket a wɔde aboɔden abo ayɛ ne ntama a ɛsensɛn mu no ma poma bi a ne ti yɛ ntakra so. Wɔde nsensanee tuntum fɛfɛ atwe anim ne nsa no wɔ asase a ɛyɛ mmerɛw so na wɔde ochre, pink ne ahabammono ahohoro ntade no — ahemfie ntadehyɛ ho adesua a ɛte sɛ mfonini wɔ asɔredan mu mfonini mu.
A detail of the painted ceiling of the J: Jainfo ɔbodan kronkronbea a ɛwɔ Sittanavasal no atifi a wɔayɛ ho adwini no ho nsɛm a ɛkɔ akyiri: lotus a ɛyɛ pink a ebue wɔ nnua a ɛyɛ ahabammono mu, aboa bi a ɔrehuruhuruw wɔ nsu no mu ne ohoni bi a ɔreboaboa nhwiren ano. Wɔtaa kenkan ɔtare no sɛ lotus moat a ɛwɔ samavasarana, ɔsoro nhyiam a Jain Tirthankara bi ka asɛmpa no mu, a anokwafo no boaboa nhwiren ano de ma.
A funerary vessel from the burial cairns: Amusie anwenne bi a efi Nilgiri nkoko so amusiei abon mu, a wɔde mfonini ahorow a wɔayɛ ho mfonini abɔ n’ano. Afeha a ɛto so dunkron mu a wotutuu Nilgiri abotan no huu nkataso a ɛte saa pii a wɔde nnipa, mmoa ne apɔnkɔsotefo ahyɛ so — nneɛma nketenkete a wɔde dɔte ayɛ a ebia ɛkyerɛ awufo asetra ne wɔn gyinabea.
A garland of about a hundred and fifty a: Nkyekyem a ɛyɛ bɛyɛ ɔha aduonum akam a Kanimethaviyar kyerɛwee, bɛyɛ aduasa ma nsase anum no mu biara.
A gold coin of Rajaraja I (985–1014 CE),: Rajaraja I (985–1014 Y.B.), a osii asɔrefie kɛse a ɛwɔ Thanjavur no sika kɔkɔɔ. Ɛkyerɛ Cholafo adehye agyiraehyɛde a wɔtaa yɛ no: ɔsebɔ a ɔte ase a Pandya mpataa abien wɔ n’afã, wɔ tumidi kyɛw ase, a ɔhene no din wɔ Nagari kasa mu — Cholafo ka sɛ wodi anafo fam.
A gold half-kahavanu of Virarajendra Cho: Sika kɔkɔɔ fã-kahavanu a Virarajendra Chola (1063–1070 Y.B.) yɛe. Na Kahavanu (a efi kahapana) yɛ sika kɔkɔɔ asɔre a ɛwɔ Sri Lanka, na Chola sika kɔkɔɔ a wɔbɔ no kodu saa gyinapɛn yi so no da bere a Cholafo dii supɔw no so adi.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Kadiya: Anwensɛm a ɛkyerɛ kwan a ɛfa Idylls Du no ho a Kadiyalur Uruthirankannanar kyerɛwee. Wɔkyerɛ bard bi a ɔwɔ yazh kɛse no kwan kɔ Thondaiman Ilanthiraiyan a ofi Kanchi; wɔ kwan so no anwensɛm no yɛ nkuraa, hyɛn gyinabea, ne nnipa ho mfonini a emu da hɔ.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Mudath: Anwensɛm a ɛkyerɛ kwan a ɛfa Idylls Du no ho a Mudathama Kanniyar kyerɛwee. Bard bi a ɔbɔ sanku (porunar) a wanya akatua pii no kyerɛ ne yɔnko sankubɔfo kwan kɔ Chola hene Karikal Valavan a ɔyɛ ɔyamyefo no nkyɛn.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Nallur: Anwensɛm a ɛkyerɛ kwan a ɛfa Idylls Du no ho a Nallur Nathathanar kyerɛwee. Bard bi a ɔbɔ yazh (sanku) ketewa no di obi foforo anim kɔ ɔpanyin Nalliyakkodan nkyɛn, na ɔka nnwontofo a wɔyɛ ahiafo ahokyere ne ɔhyew a obi a ɔyɛ ɔyamyefo wɔ no ho asɛm.
A guide poem of the Ten Idylls by Perunk: Anwensɛm a ɛkyerɛ kwan a ɛfa Idylls Du no ho a Perunkausikanar kyerɛwee. Wɔkyerɛ wɔn a wɔkyinkyin (koothar) kwan kɔ ɔpanyin Nannan nkyɛn; wɔhyɛ anwensɛm no ho afahyɛ sɛ ɛkyere mmepɔw so nnyigyei pii.
A large storage jar associated with Adic: Toa kɛse bi a wɔde nneɛma gu a ɛne Adichanallur wɔ abusuabɔ. Ná nkuku a ɛdɔɔso a wɔde aburow, nsu ne nneɛma afoforo gu mu; wɔ amusiei no, na nkuku a ne kɛse te sɛɛ nso betumi ayɛ nkuku. Asɛmfua “dolio” ma yɛkae dolium, Roma wiase no mu toa kɛse a wɔde nneɛma gu mu no.
A large, round-bellied funerary urn from: Ayie ahina kɛse bi a ne yafunu yɛ kurukuruwa a efi Adichanallur. Nkuku a ɛte sɛɛ betumi agyina atenten asen abofra, na sɛ wɔbɛyɛ no hwehwɛ ahokokwaw kɛse: Sangam anwensɛm akyerɛwfo kasa kyerɛ ɔnwemfo a ɔyɛɛ nkuku te sɛ கலம்செய் கோவே — “O hene a ɔte nkukuo mu”.
A lead coin from Andipatti bearing a leg: Kɔbere sika bi a efi Andipatti a anansesɛm bi wɔ so wɔ Tamil-Brahmi kasa mu. Sɛ ahene baasa a wɔde abotiri abɔ wɔn no da nkyɛn a, ɛhɔnom mpanyimfo a wɔtraa ase wɔ Sangam bere so no de sika a wɔde kɔbere ne kɔbere ayɛ mae, na Tamil-Brahmi anansesɛm ahorow a ɛfa ho no boa ma wɔde din frɛ saa sodifo yi.
A line drawing of the vimana and a pilla: Vimana ne Brihadisvara Asɔredan no asa a wɔde adum ayɛ ho mfonini.
A love poem of the Ten Idylls by Kapilar: Ɔdɔ anwensɛm a ɛfa Idylls Du no ho a Kapilar kyerɛwee, a wɔde sii bepɔw (kurinji) asase so. Atetesɛm ka sɛ wɔkyerɛwee sɛ wɔde bɛkyerɛkyerɛ atifi fam hene bi Tamilfo ɔdɔ anwensɛm a ɛyɛ fɛ; agye din sɛ ɛbɔ nhwiren aduɔkron akron din.
A modern artist’s imagining of a busy ha: Nnɛyi mfoniniyɛfo bi a ɔyɛ hyɛn gyinabea a adagyew nnim a po so ahyɛn, gua ne abantenten wom ho mfonini wɔ n’adwenem, wɔ nkyerɛkyerɛmu ahorow a ɛwɔ Silappathikaram ne Pattinappalai no akyi. Ɛnyɛ sɛnea na kurow no te ankasa ho adanse.
A modern sketch imagining ships and buil: Nnɛyi mfonini bi a ɛkyerɛ po so ahyɛn ne adan a ɛwɔ tete hyɛn gyinabea hɔ ho mfonini. Te sɛ Puhar a wɔsan si no foforo biara no, ɛkyerɛkyerɛ nhoma mu nkyerɛkyerɛmu ahorow ase; wonnim sɛnea wɔahyehyɛ hyɛn gyinabea no nyinaa.
A name linked with Nedunalvadai and Tiru: Edin a ɛne Nedunalvadai ne Tirumurukarruppatai wɔ abusuabɔ wɔ Idylls Du no mu — ɛwom sɛ ebia ɛyɛ anwensɛm akyerɛwfo bɛboro biako dea wɔ mmere ahorow mu de. Akyiri yi anansesɛm ka sɛnea ɔpowee sɛ ɔde n’atemmu a ɛfa anwensɛm bi ho bɛma Shiva mpo wɔ Pandya ahemfie no ho asɛm: ɛyɛ adwene mu akokoduru ho sɛnkyerɛnne, na ɛnyɛ abakɔsɛm mu asɛm bi.
A Note on the Evidence: Adanse no Ho Nsɛm a Wɔakyerɛw
A palm-leaf manuscript from the museum’s: Nsaano nkyerɛwee a wɔde mmɛw ahaban ayɛ a efi tete nneɛma akorae no nneɛma a wɔaboaboa ano.
A Pandya coin of the “massa” type. Massa: Pandya sika a ɛyɛ “massa” su. Massa yɛ din a wɔde frɛɛ mfinimfini mmere mu kɔbere sika a ɛkyerɛ sɛ obi gyina hɔ wɔ ɔfã biako na ɔte hɔ wɔ ɔfã foforo — ɔkwan a Cholafo trɛwee na Pandyafo ne Sri Lanka ahemfo toaa so.
A Pandya coin showing a standing king wi: Pandya sika bi a ɛkyerɛ ɔhene bi a ogyina hɔ a ɔwɔ mpataa agyiraehyɛde. Sodifo a ogyina hɔ mfonini a Chola kɔbere sika a wɔde yɛɛ no ​​ma wohuu no no, Pandyafo no gyee bere a wɔn tumi san bae wɔ afeha a ɛto so 13 mu no.
A Pandya coin with the twin fish and a b: Pandya sika bi a mpataa mmanoma ne nantwinini bi wom. Mpataa abien abien no bɛyɛɛ Pandya agyiraehyɛde a ɛtra hɔ daa, a wodi adwini wɔ anwensɛm no Madurai frankaa so na wɔde bɔɔ sika bɛboro mfe apem koraa.
A pillared hall today: Asa a wɔde adum ayɛ nnɛ
A pipeline of terracotta rings, set one: Pipeline a wɔde dɔte nkaa ayɛ, a wɔde asisi biako atifi wɔ abansoro anan mu, a ɛdaa adi wɔ Korkai fam tutu no mu. Dɔte paipu a wɔde ogya ayɛ ne abura a wɔde yɛ ring te sɛ eyi de nsu na ɛkɔe wɔ nkurow a ɛwɔ abakɔsɛm mu Tamil man a edi kan no mu —a ɛyɛ hyɛn gyinabea a adagyew nnim ho mfiridwuma a wɔyɛ no da biara da no fã.
A poem of the Ten Idylls by Kadiyalur Ur: Anwensɛm a ɛfa Idylls Du no ho a Kadiyalur Uruthirankannanar kyerɛwee, a ɛkamfo Chola hene Karikal Valavan ne ne hyɛn gyinabea kurow Kaveripoompattinam (Puhar) a nnipa pii wɔ hɔ no, a emu po so ahyɛn, gua ahorow, ne afahyɛ ahorow wom.
A poem of the Ten Idylls by Nakkeerar. D: Anwensɛm bi a ɛfa Idylls Du no ho a Nakkeerar kyerɛwee. Wɔ awɔw bere mu atifi fam mframa tenten a ɛyɛ nwini no mu no, ɔhemmaa bi kɔn dɔ ne kunu bere a ɔhene no hwɛ n’asraafo a wɔapirapira wɔ ɔko nsraban bi mu no.
A portrait coin of the Chera king Kuttuv: Chera hene Kuttuvan Kotai mfonini sika bi, a ɔbɔɔ ne din wɔ Tamil-Brahmi kasa mu. Wɔ Makkotai sika no ho no, dwetɛ nsɛmma nhoma a wɔntaa nhu yi — ebia Romafo mfonini sika a ɛnam aguadi so ba no na ɛkanyan no — ka Indiafo sika a edi kan a wɔde kyerɛ sodifo bi anim no ho.
A potsherd inscribed in Tamil-Brahmi, fo: Nkukuo a wɔakyerɛw so wɔ Tamil-Brahmi kasa mu, a wohuu wɔ Tissamaharama wɔ Sri Lanka kesee fam na wɔkyerɛw no bɛyɛ afeha a ɛto so 2 A.Y.B. Sɛ wɔkyerɛw nkuku a ɛwɔ akyirikyiri fi Tamil asasepɔn no so wɔ Tamil kasa mu a, ɛkyerɛ Tamil aguadifo a wɔreyɛ adwuma wɔ po no atifi wɔ abakɔsɛm bere a edi kan no mu.
A rare book from the first decades of Ta: Nhoma a wɔntaa nhu a efi Tamil nhoma tintim mfe du du a edi kan no mu, bere a na wɔde nkyerɛwee a wɔagye din a wɔakora so wɔ mmɛw nhaban so no reyɛ nea edi kan no.
A rare volume digitised from CICT’s arch: Nhoma bi a wɔntaa nhu a wɔde digitized fii CICT’s archive na wɔkoraa so sɛ wɔmfa nsua. Tete nneɛma akorae no so ahwɛfo de nhoma a wɔahyehyɛ ho nsɛm nyinaa bɛka ho.
A Sangam-age Chola coin with a tiger and: Cholafo sika a wɔde yɛɛ Sangam bere so a ɔsebɔ ne asono wom. Cholafo sika a edi kan a ne fã kɛse no ara yɛ kɔbere no gyina ɔsebɔ no so — agyiraehyɛde koro no ara a na ahemman Cholafo no de bɛkɔ mfe apem akyi. Ná Uraiyur ne Kaveripoompattinam yɛ wɔn mmeae akɛse.
A Sangam-age Pandya coin, typically a sm: Pandya sika a wɔde yɛɛ Sangam bere so, a mpɛn pii no ɛyɛ kɔbere ahinanan ketewaa bi a asono wɔ ɔfã biako na apataa a wɔayɛ no sɛnea wɔpɛ wɔ ɔfã foforo. Ná sika a ɛtete saa di akɔneaba wɔ Madurai, Pandya ahenkurow a wodi ho afahyɛ wɔ Maduraikkanchi no mu ne ne mpɔtam.
A scholarly study of government, adminis: Nhomanimfo nhwehwɛmu a wɔyɛe wɔ nniso, nniso, ne asetra mu asetra ho wɔ Tamil man a na ɛwɔ Sangam bere so no mu.
A second coin of the Kongu Cheras. Compa: Kongu Cherasfo sika a ɛto so abien. Fa abien no toto ho: sika a wɔde nsa bɔ no gu ahorow wɔ sɛnea wɔbɔ, sɛnea wɔsɛe no ne sɛnea wotwa mu, na nsonsonoe a ɛte saa boa sika ho animdefo ma wɔhyehyɛ nsɛmpɔw ahorow na wohu bere tenten a sika no traa hɔ.
A second image of the four-armed, seated: Ganesha a ɔwɔ nsa anan a ɔte hɔ no honi a ɛto so abien. Fa ne nsusuwii, agude ne sɛnea ɛdannan dua no toto nea edi kan no ho: wɔ Silpa Sastras no mmara a wɔkyɛ mu no, odumgyafo ne adwumayɛbea biara gyaw n’ankasa nsa.
A selection drawn from the Thirukkural,: Nsɛm a wɔapaw a wonya fii Thirukkural mu, a ɛboaboa nsɛm abien a wɔbɛkae ano ma akenkanfo.
A separate photographing of the opening: Mfonini a ɛyɛ soronko a ɛfa nhaban a ebue bundle 579 D, Maduraikkanchi, no ho.
Shaiva ɔhotefo bi, nsa a wɔaka abom wɔ ɔsom mu. Chola ahemfo no hyɛɛ Nayanmarfo aduosia abiɛsa a Sekkizhar kaa wɔn asetra ho asɛm wɔ Periya Puranam mu no anuonyam, na wɔde wɔn kɔbere ahoni sisi asɔredan ahorow mu na wɔde kɔɔ afahyɛ ahorow mu.
A sherd illustrated in Vimala Begley’s 1: Ade a ɛyɛ asinasin a wɔayɛ ho mfonini wɔ Vimala Begley nhwehwɛmu a ɔyɛe wɔ 1983 mu wɔ Arikamedu bere a ɔne no dae ho no mu. Bere a Begley san hwehwɛɛ nsensanee a wotutuu no mu no, ɔkae sɛ atrae no fii ase bɛyɛ afeha a ɛto so abiɛsa A.Y.B. Ne nna no da so ara yɛ nhomanimfo nkyerɛase.
A sherd of an urn found in 2004, decorat: Kuruwa bi asinasin bi a wohuu wɔ afe 2004 mu, a wɔde mfonini a wɔde ayɛ asiesie a ɔbea bi a ogyina hɔ wɔ nsusuwso ahorow a wɔtaa kenkan sɛ aburow nnua, ɔkraman, krane ne akokɔsrade mu. Nhomanimfo ahu ɛna nyamewa bi a odi kan wɔ ne mu — ebinom, sɛnea sini no ka no, Kotravai, Sangam anwensɛm mu ɔko nyamewa no kannifo. A short illustrated guide for visitors:: Akwankyerɛ tiawa a mfonini wom ma nsrahwɛfo: nea Sangam anwensɛm no yɛ, sɛnea wɔahyehyɛ no akuwakuw, ne sɛnea akam ne puram anwensɛm ne nsase anum no yɛ adwuma.

Agriculture remains an important part of: Kuadwuma da so ara yɛ Tamil Nadu sikasɛm ne nkuraase asetra fã titiriw. Nnuadewa atitiriw bi ne aburow, asikre, kotoku, atoko, atoko, ne atoko, na ɛsono sɛnea wodua no sɛnea asase, osutɔ, nsu a wɔde gugu nnɔbae so, ne nea wɔhwehwɛ wɔ gua so te. Nnɛyi akuafo de atetesɛm mu nimdeɛ ne nnɛyi mfiridwuma a wɔaka abom di dwuma, a trakta, mfiri a wɔde twa, aba a wɔatu mpɔn, pɔmpɛ a wɔde gugu nnɔbae so, ne akwan a wɔfa so hwɛ asase so yiye ka ho. Nsuo a wɔde gugu nnɔbaeɛ so ne akwan foforɔ a ɛmma nsuo nsɛe no bɛtumi aboa ama wɔadi nsuo a ɛho yɛ na ho dwuma wɔ kuayɛ nhyehyɛeɛ a ɛfata mu. Akuafo nso hyia nsɛnnennen te sɛ osu a ɛntɔ daa, ɔpɛ, nneɛma a wɔde yɛ adwuma ho ka a ɛkɔ soro, adwumayɛfo a wɔn ho yɛ na, ne gua so nneɛma bo a ɛresakra. Enti Tamil Nadu’s kuayɛ agyapade gyina hɔ ma abakɔsɛm tenten a ɛfa sɛnea wɔyɛ nsakrae wɔ mpɔtam hɔ nneɛma a atwa yɛn ho ahyia tebea horow mu ne ɔfã bi a ɛrenya nkɔso a ɛyɛ nnɛyi sikasɛm ne wim tebea ho nhyɛso ho dwuma.
Agriculture was an important source of f: Ná kuayɛ yɛ aduan, asetrade, ne sikasɛm mu dwumadi a ɛho hia wɔ tete Tamilfo asetra mu. Sangam nhoma ahorow a wɔtaa de bata bere a na ɛwɔ hɔ bɛyɛ afe 300 A.Y.B.–300 Y.B. Tamil anwensɛm akyerɛwfo de nsase ahorow bataa asetra akwan soronko ho. Ná Marutham asase no gyina hɔ ma kuayɛ nsase a ɛsow aba, baabi a na aburow a wodua ne kuayɛ afoforo da nsow no. Akuafo paw nnɔbae sɛnea asase no tebea te, osutɔ, ne nsu a ɛwɔ hɔ. Aburow, atoko, asikre, atoko, kotoku, ne sesame ka nnɔbae a wɔkaa ho asɛm wɔ tete Tamil kuayɛ ho nhwehwɛmu ahorow mu no ho. Ná kuayɛ gyina nnipa adwuma, mmoa tumi, ne mpɔtam hɔ nneɛma a atwa yɛn ho ahyia ho nimdeɛ so. Nhoma mu adanse ma yenya nhumu a ɛsom bo wɔ kuayɛ asetra ho, ɛwom sɛ ɛsɛ sɛ wɔkyerɛ ase ka fam tutu ne abakɔsɛm mu nhwehwɛmu ho de.

Wɔakyerɛw atetesɛm mu nsu a wɔde fa nsu mu ahorow pii ho asɛm wɔ Tamil Nadu, a madai, madagu, thumpu ne kumizhi ka ho. Ná ɛsono sɛnea wɔyɛɛ wɔn pɛpɛɛpɛ ne sɛnea wɔyɛe. Nhwɛso biako a ɛyɛ anigye titiriw ne kumizhi nhyehyɛe, nsu a wɔde fa nsu mu titiriw a ɛne atetesɛm mu nsu a wɔde di dwuma wɔ tank mu no wɔ abusuabɔ. Nsu a wɔde fa nsu mu boaa akuafo ma wogyaee nsu bere a ɛho hia, sen sɛ wɔbɛma nsu a ɛwɔ nsukorabea no mu ada mpan a wontumi nni so, na ɛboaa nsu a wɔahyehyɛ no kyekyɛ denam akwan a ɛsom kuayɛ mmeae ahorow so. Nkyerɛwee a ɛda so ara wɔ hɔ no yɛ adanse a ɛsom bo titiriw a ɛkyerɛ sɛ nsu a wɔde gugu nnɔbae so yi ne dwuma a edi wɔ kuayɛ nsase a ɛsakra no.

Kallanai stands across the Kaveri about: Kallanai gyina Kaveri no atifi bɛyɛ kilomita dunum fi Tiruchirappalli, Srirangam supɔw no apuei fam, baabi a asubɔnten no fi ase kyekyɛ ma delta no. Ɛnyɛ abura a wɔkora nneɛma so na mmom anicut: abura a ɛma asubɔnten no siw ano araa ma ɛdan ne nsu kɔ nsuten mu. Tete ade titiriw no yɛ ɔfasu a ɛba fam a wɔde abo a wɔantwa a ne tenten bɛyɛ mita 330; wosii abɔntenban a ɛyɛ ahinanan ne mframa a wɔde fa mu a wohu nnɛ no wɔ so wɔ afeha a ɛto so dunkron ne aduonu no mu.
Kallanai was built without mortar, on th: Wɔkyekyee Kallanai a na wɔmfa atɛkyɛ nni mu, wɔ asubɔnten no ankasa anhwea a ɛsakra so. Wɔn a wosisii no bobɔɔ abo akɛse a wontwitwaa mu guu Kaveri no mu; bere a nsu a ɛreworo so no reprapra anhwea no afi wɔn ase no abo no memee, na wɔboaboaa pii guu so kosii sɛ akuwakuw no gyinaa asase a ɛyɛ den so. Dɔte ne nsuyiri no mu nsu a ɛyɛ fĩ hyɛɛ nsonsonoe no ma na ɛkyekyeree abo no yɛɛ no ​​akwanside biako a nsu ntumi nkɔ mu: ɔfasu a ɛba fam na ɛtrɛw a ne tenten bɛyɛ mita 330 na ne tɛtrɛtɛ bɛyɛ mita 20, a wɔde ato nhama a ɛyɛ kyinhyia a kyerɛwtohɔ no de toto ɔwɔ a ɔwea ho. Ɛyɛ anicut, ɛnyɛ atare — ɛma asubɔnten no so sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a ɛbɛma ne nsu akɔ nsuten no mu, na ɛma nea aka no twam.
Kallanai, also known as the Grand Anicut: Kallanai a wɔsan frɛ no Grand Anicut no yɛ nsu ho mfiridwuma a wɔde di dwuma wɔ amanne kwan so ho nhwɛso a ɛyɛ nwonwa sen biara wɔ Tamil Nadu no mu biako. Egyina Kaveri Asubɔnten no agya, na wɔkyerɛ sɛ Karikala Chola, Cholafo hene bi a odii kan bae no na efi atetesɛm mu. Wɔyɛɛ ɔdan no titiriw sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a ɛbɛdan asubɔnten mu nsu akɔ nsu a wɔde gugu nnɔbae so sen sɛ wɔde nsu besie wɔ atare mu kɛkɛ. Atare no boa ma wɔkyekyɛɛ Kaveri nsu no wɔ asase a ɛsow aba a wɔyɛ kua wɔ delta no so, baabi a aburow a wodua bɛyɛɛ nea ɛho hia titiriw no. Abo a ɛba fam na ɛtrɛw no ne asubɔnten no mu nsu a ɛsen no yɛ adwuma de kyerɛ nsu kwan kɔ nsu a wɔde gugu nnɔbae so. Nea ɛnte sɛ nnɛyi abura a ɛkorɔn no, na n’atirimpɔw titiriw ne sɛ wɔbɛdan nsu na wɔakyekyɛ. Kallanai gyina hɔ ma abusuabɔ a emu yɛ den a ɛda asubɔnten sohwɛ, kuayɛ mu nneɛma a wɔyɛ ne nnipa a wɔtra Tamil mantam mu ntam. Dwuma a ɛkɔ so di wɔ nsu a wɔde gugu nnɔbae so no nso kyerɛ sɛnea atetesɛm mu mfiridwuma adan betumi akɔ so ayɛ nea mfaso wɔ so denam akyiri yi a wɔbɛhwɛ so na wɔasakra no so. Nnuan a ɛne Kurinji wɔ abusuabɔ: thinai (foxtail millet), ɛwo, wuram nnuaba, aburow a wɔde bamboo ayɛ wɔ baabi a bamboo no nhwiren wɔ hɔ, kwae mu nnuadewa ne ntini, nam a efi abɔmmɔ mu, ne nhabannuru ne nnuaba a wotumi di. Sangam literature is the earliest body o: Sangam nhoma ne Tamil anwensɛm a edi kan koraa. Wɔ atetesɛm mu no, wɔaboaboa ano ayɛ no nhoma akɛse abien: Anthologies Awotwe (Ettuthokai) ne Idylls Du (Pattuppattu). Wɔka bom kora anwensɛm bɛboro mpem abien a anwensɛm akyerɛwfo ɔhaha pii kyerɛwee, a mmea, ahene, ne nnwontofo a wɔkyinkyin ka ho.
Sangam poems already speak of painters a: Sangam anwensɛm ka mfoniniyɛfo ne asa ahorow a wɔayɛ ho mfonini ho asɛm dedaw: ஓவியர் a wɔde nsensanee fɛfɛ twetwe mfonini, ne ஓவியச் செந்நூல், mfoniniyɛ ho asɛm. Nea ɛda so ara wɔ afasu so no fi ase wɔ afeha a ɛto so 7–9 mu — wɔ Pallava asɔredan ahorow ne Jainfo ɔbodan a ɛwɔ Sittanavasal mu — na ɛfa Cholafo mfonini akɛse a ɛwɔ Thanjavur no mu kɔ Nayakfo afasu a ɛhyerɛn ne Tanjore ntama a wɔde sika kɔkɔɔ ayɛ a ɛwɔ afeha a ɛto so 17–19 mu no so. Tamil farmers traditionally cultivated c: Ná Tamil akuafo dua nnɔbae a ɛfata asase ahorow, osutɔ kwan, ne nsu a wɔde ma. Ná aburow ho hia titiriw wɔ mmeae a ɛsow aba na nsu pa wɔ hɔ, bere a na atoko te sɛ kambu ne varagu fata ma kuayɛ mmeae ahorow a ɛhɔ yɛ kusuu. Tamil seafarers sailed with the monsoon: Tamilfo po so akwantufo de po so hyɛn a mframa a ɛbɔ wɔ osutɔbere mu fi ansa na bere a wɔtaa bɔ no reba no. Wɔ Cholafo ase no, po so ahyɛn twaa Bengal Po no: Wɔakyerɛw Rajendra I akwantu a ɔkɔɔ Srivijaya, bɛyɛ afe 1025 Y.B. The Jambai inscription in Villupuram dis: Jambai nkyerɛwee a ɛwɔ Villupuram mantam mu no to din “Satiyaputo Atiyan Netuman Anci”, a ɛde Atiyaman mpanyimfo no ne Satiyaputa a wɔaka wɔn ho asɛm wɔ Ashoka ahyɛde ahorow mu no bata ho.
The Kadai Ezhu Vallalgal — Seven Great P: Kadai Ezhu Vallalgal — Aboafo Kɛse baason
The Kailasanatha Temple, a Pallava-perio: Kailasanatha Asɔredan, Pallava bere so abo asɔredan, a asɔredan nketewa a ɛtoatoa so wɔ ne ho.
The kalayam, the everyday Tamil clay pot: Kalayam, Tamilfo dɔte kuku a wɔde yɛ da biara da. Ne nipadua a ɛyɛ kurukuruwa ne ne kɔn teateaa no ma nsu yɛ nwini na ɛnyɛ den sɛ wɔbɛsoa, na wɔda so ara tow kalaayam gu ɔnwemfo no ntwahonan so na wɔtow wɔ akuraa ase fononoo mu —a ɛyɛ abusuabɔ a ɛte ase a ɛne nkuku a wotutuu wɔ Tamil mmeae no ntam.
The Kallanai, or Grand Anicut, across th: Wɔkyekyeree Kallanai, anaa Grand Anicut, a ɛwɔ Kaveri atifi — a wɔkyerɛ sɛ Chola hene Karikala na ɔkyerɛwee — sɛ wɔde bɛhyɛ asubɔnten no mu nsu ho nhyehyɛe na wɔadan akɔ nsuten mu de agugu nnɔbae so. Ɛmaa Kaveri asubɔnten no yɛɛ Tamil Nadu nsase akɛse a wodua aburow no mu biako, na ɛda so ara som ne nsu a wɔde gugu nnɔbae so nnɛ. The Kanchipuram silk saree is one of the: Kanchipuram sirikyi saree yɛ Tamil Nadu amammerɛ ntama a wɔagye din sen biara no mu biako. Saa saree yi fi Kanchipuram, abakɔsɛm mu nwene beae bi, na agye din wɔ ntama a ɛyɛ dɛ a wɔde sirikyi ayɛ, zari adwuma a ɛyɛ nwonwa, ahye a ɛsono emu biara, ne nsusuwso a ɛyɛ nwonwa ho. Amanne kwan so mfonini ahorow no bi ne asɔredan abantenten, akɔre, mango, nhwiren, ne geometric mfonini ahorow. Wɔde sirikyi asaawa nawe saree no, na wɔde zari nhama a ɛyɛ sika kɔkɔɔ anaa dwetɛ kɔla na ɛde ahosiesie a ɛyɛ fɛ ka ho. Kanchipuram silk saree ahorow wɔ beae titiriw wɔ Tamilfo ayeforohyia ahorow, nyamesom guasodeyɛ ahorow, afahyɛ ahorow, ne mmere titiriw afoforo mu. Nwene no hwehwɛ ahokokwaw kɛse, titiriw bere a wɔde atetesɛm akwan a wɔfa so ka nipadua no bom, ɔhye, ne pallu no bom no. Adwinni no nyaa nkɔso wɔ awo ntoatoaso pii mu, na afe pɔtee a wɔde sii hɔ no nyɛ nea wɔde sii hɔ wɔ abakɔsɛm mu. Kancheepuram Silk nyaa Geographical Indication (GI) agyede wɔ afe 2005. Ɛnnɛ, saree no gyina hɔ ma Tamil Nadu ntama agyapade, nsaanodwuma a wɔn ho akokwaw, ne atetesɛm mu nwene mpɔtam hɔfo asetra a ɛkɔ so.
The Kandangi saree is a traditional cott: Kandangi saree yɛ amammerɛ kwan so ntama a wɔde kotoku ayɛ a ɛne Chettinad mantam no wɔ abusuabɔ, titiriw Karaikudi ne mmeae a ɛbemmɛn hɔ. Wogye tom wɔ ne checks a ɛyɛ den, nsensanee, hye a ɛsono emu biara, ne kɔla ahorow a emu yɛ den, a kɔkɔɔ, sinapi, borɔdɔma, ne dɔte bruu ka ho. Sɛnea wɔtaa yɛ no, na ne ntama a ɛyɛ den a wɔde kotoku ayɛ no fata sɛ wɔde di dwuma daa, na na ɛda ahwehwɛde ahorow a mfaso wɔ so a ɛwɔ da biara da ntade mu adi. Kandangi nwene gyina hɔ ma afɛfɛde ne ntama ho nimdeɛ soronko a ɛwɔ Chettinad mantam no mu. Ne nsusuwso ne kɔla ahorow a wɔaka abom no ma ɛda nsow wɔ South India saree atetesɛm afoforo pii ho. Nea ɛka nneɛma a wɔyɛ no ho ne sɛ wosiesie asaawa, wɔhyehyɛ nhama wɔ ntamadan no so, wɔpam ntama no, na wowie ahye no na wowie. Aban nsaanodwuma ho nneɛma ka atetesɛm no ho asɛm sɛ atra hɔ bɛboro mfe 150 ni, ɛwom sɛ afe pɔtee a wofii ase no da so ara yɛ nea wontumi nsi pi de. Kandangi sarees nyaa GI agyedeɛ wɔ afe 2019 mu, ɛboaa ma wɔhunuu na wɔkoraa wɔn mpɔtam hɔ nipasu ne atetesɛm nsaanodwuma so.

The Kaveri in spate below the Grand Anic: Kaveri a ɛrehuruw wɔ Grand Anicut ase. Anicut no danee saa akyɛde no yɛɛ no ​​nhyehyɛe a wɔhwɛ so, na delta no bɛyɛɛ Tamil man no aburow kuruwa.

The Koorainadu saree is associated with: Koorainadu saree no ne Koorainadu a ɛbɛn Mayiladuthurai wɔ Tamil Nadu no wɔ abusuabɔ. Ɛne ayeforohyia ntade a wɔhyɛ wɔ amanne kwan so ne amammerɛ mu ntease a ɛwɔ ntama mu wɔ Tamilfo aware amanne mu no wɔ abusuabɔ titiriw. Amanneɛ kwan so ahorow no bi ne ntama a wɔde sirikyi ne sirikyi-cotton ayɛ, a ɛsono sɛnea wɔayɛ ne nneɛma a wɔde di dwuma sɛnea ɔkwan pɔtee a wɔfa so yɛ ne atirimpɔw pɔtee no te. Saree no da dwuma a ntade a wɔanwene di wɔ abusua guasodeyɛ ahorow a ɛho hia mu ne ntama atetesɛm a wɔde ma wɔ awo ntoatoaso ahorow ntam no adi. Ne hwɛbea, ntama, ne nneɛma a wɔde asiesie no betumi ayɛ soronko, enti ɛsɛ sɛ wɔkyerɛw nhwɛso ahorow ankorankoro sɛnea wɔasisi ankasa sen sɛ wobesusuw sɛ Koorainadu saree biara di nhyehyɛe koro akyi. Wɔmfaa afe pɔtee a saa atetesɛm yi fii ase no nsi hɔ pintinn. Koorainadu sarees da so ara yɛ asɛmti a ɛsom bo a wɔde hwehwɛ abusuabɔ a ɛda ntade, ɔmantam nipasu, nsaanodwuma, ne amanne kwan so asetra ntam wɔ Tamil Nadu.
The Kovai Kora cotton saree is associate: Kovai Kora cotton saree no ne Coimbatore ne ne mpɔtam a wɔyɛ ntama a atwa ho ahyia no wɔ abusuabɔ. Wɔde kotoku na ɛyɛe, na wɔkyerɛ ho anisɔ wɔ ne fɛ a wɔmfa nyɛ hwee, sɛnea ɛyɛ fɛ, ne atetesɛm mu hye a ɛwɔ hɔ no ho. Sɛ wɔde toto sirikyi saree a wɔasiesie no kɛse ho a, Kora ntama a wɔde kotoku ayɛ no taa si sɛnea kotoku te fi awosu mu, sɛnea wɔhyɛ no yiye, ne sɛnea wɔayɛ no anifere kwan so so dua. Saree no da hia a ɛho hia sɛ wɔyɛ kotoku, asaawa a wɔyɛ, nwene, ne ntama a wɔtɔn wɔ Tamil Nadu no adi. Sɛ wɔbɛyɛ nsaanodwuma saree a, ɛhwehwɛ sɛ wɔde ahwɛyiye siesie warp ne weft nhama na wɔde ahokokwaw di dwuma wɔ ntamadan no mu. Kora kotoku fata ma mmere ahorow, a da biara da ntade ne nhyiam ahorow a wɔyɛ wɔ ɔkwan a ɛfata so ka ho. Kovai Kora Cotton nyaa GI agyedeɛ wɔ afe 2008. Wɔnnya nsii afe pɔtee a wɔde sii hɔ, nanso atetesɛm no da so ara yɛ nhwɛsoɔ a ɛho hia a ɛkyerɛ ɔman no agyapadeɛ ahodoɔ a ɛfa kotokuo nwene ho.

The last leaf of the bundle: Ahaban a etwa to a ɛwɔ bundle no mu

The literary image of ancient Tamil mari: Tete Tamilfo po so yiyedi ho mfonini a wɔakyerɛw wɔ nhoma mu.
The long pillared cloister that encloses: Asɔredan tenten a adum wɔ so a ɛka Brihadisvara asɔredan no adiwo ho hyia, a lingam ahorow a ɛtoatoa so a wɔde asisi ne fam. Wɔde mfonini ahorow a ɛyɛ anigye na ɛyɛɛ n’afasu ho adwini wɔ Nayak bere so — ha na Shiva’s pot-bellied ganas, n’asomfo a wɔyɛ dwarf a wodi agoru — wɔ Tamilfo nsɛm a wɔakyerɛw so. Wɔ mfonini ahorow a ɛtete saa a wɔyɛe akyiri yi akyi no, wɔ ɔkwan a atwa kronkronbea no ho ahyia no mu no, asɔredan no mfitiase Cholafo mfonini ahorow no da hɔ.
The longest of the Ten Idylls, by Mangud: Idylls Du no mu nea ɛware sen biara, a Mangudi Maruthanar kyerɛwee, a wɔkyerɛw kɔmaa Pandya hene Nedunchezhiyan. Ɛka Madurai kurow kɛse no ho asɛm fi anɔpa kosi anadwo na ɛkae ɔhene no brɛoo sɛ wiase anuonyam nyinaa twam.

The lotus pool of Sittanavasal, the Pall: Lotus ɔtare a ɛwɔ Sittanavasal, Pallava nyamewa a ɔwɔ Panamalai, Cholafo mfonini ahorow ne Nayakfo afasu ho mfonini ahorow a ɛwɔ Asɔredan Kɛse a ɛwɔ Thanjavur no ho, ne Tanjore mfonini ahorow a wɔde sika kɔkɔɔ ayɛ.
The Madurai Sungudi saree is a tradition: Madurai Sungudi saree yɛ amammerɛ kwan so ntama a wɔde kotoku ayɛ a ɛne Madurai, abakɔsɛm mu amammerɛ ne aguadi beae bi a ɛwɔ Tamil Nadu no wɔ abusuabɔ. Ɛda nsow denam ne nsusuwso a ɛyɛ nsensanee, ne mfonini ahorow a ɛyɛ kɔla ahorow, ne atetesɛm mu akwan a wɔfa so kyekyere nneɛma anaasɛ wɔde kɔla a wɔde siw ano no so. Wɔkyekyere ntama no afã nketenkete anaa wɔbɔ ho ban bere a wɔreyɛ kɔla no na ama wɔayɛ nsusuwso soronko bere a wɔabue ade no mu no. Wobu Sungudi ntama sɛ ɛsom bo esiane sɛnea ɛyɛ fɛ, ntama a wɔde kotoku ayɛ a emu yɛ hare, ne sɛnea ɛfata ma da biara da ne afahyɛ ntade nti. Adwinni no ka nimdeɛ a ɛfa ntama a wosiesie, akwan a wɔfa so kyekyere, kɔla a wɔde yɛ, ne nea wɔde wie ho bom. Wɔnkyekyeree n’abakɔsɛm mu mfiase wɔ afe biako a wɔakyerɛw ho asɛm a ahobammɔ wom a efii ase no ho. Madurai Sungudi nyaa GI agyedeɛ wɔ afe 2005 mu, na ɔgyee sɛ ɔne ɔmantam no wɔ abusuabɔ. Atetesɛm no kyerɛ sɛnea Tamil adwumfo de nnuru soronko a wɔde yɛ ntama ne nneɛma a wɔyɛ a wɔde asi hɔ wɔ mpɔtam hɔ no yɛɛ ntama ho mfonini soronko.
The masonry arches that now crown the an: Abo a wɔde ayɛ apon a mprempren ɛyɛ tete abura no abotiri no. Britania mfiridwumayɛfo a wosuaa Kallanai ho ade wɔ afeha a ɛto so dunkron no mu no ani gyee ho: Owura Arthur Cotton suaa ade fii ne fapem ahorow mu ansa na ɔresi Atifi Anicut atwa Kollidam wɔ 1836 mu, na Richard Baird Smith kamfoo no wɔ 1850 mfe no mu sɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ nwonwa a ɛkɔɔ so mfehaha pii. The Meenakshi Amman Temple, historic str: Meenakshi Amman Asɔredan, abakɔsɛm mu mmɔnten, nyamesom atetesɛm, ne nhoma ne amammerɛ mu nneyɛe a ɛkɔ so no de nnɛyi Madurai ne n’abakɔsɛm a ɛware no bata ho.
The memorial hall to Karikal Chozhan at: Nkaedi dan a wɔde ma Karikal Chozhan wɔ Kallanai, a Tamil Nadu Aban maa so. Wɔkae Karikalan, Pattinappalai ne Porunarruppadaifo ɔbran no wɔ Tamilfo atetesɛm mu sɛ ɔhene a ɔhyɛɛ Kaverifo ase. Akyiri yi Cholafo anwensɛm te sɛ Kulothunga Cholan Ula, ne ahemman ahorow a wɔkyerɛ sɛ wofi ne mu ho nkyerɛwee ahorow no de ne ho anuonyam ma sɛ ɔmaa Kaveri’s banks no kɔɔ soro.

The monuments themselves, with Pallava i: Nkaedum no ankasa, a wɔakyerɛw Pallava nkyerɛwee ne ahemfo abodin ahorow wɔ so.
The most celebrated of the Seven Great P: Wɔn a wodi ho afahyɛ sen biara wɔ Patrons Akɛse baason no mu. Tamilfo atetesɛm kae sɛ ɔde n’ankasa teaseɛnam maa jasmine (mullai) creeper a na onni biribiara a ɔbɛforo — ayamye a ɛkɔ akyiri sen nnipa kodu abɔde mu wiase. Wɔakora n’adamfofa a ɔne anwensɛm kyerɛwfo Kapilar nyae, Parambu Nadu a ɔbɔɔ ho ban fii ahene baasa a wɔde abotiri ahyɛ wɔn so no ho, ne ne mmabea Angavai ne Sangavai (Purananuru 112) kwadwom (Purananuru 112) no so wɔ Sangam anwensɛm mu; teaseɛnam ho asɛm no yɛ nea eye sɛ wɔkenkan sɛ nhoma mu atetesɛm.
The mountains and the land around them,: Mmepɔw ne asase a atwa wɔn ho ahyia, anadwo fã wɔ awɔw bere mu. Ne nyame ne Murugan (Seyon), na ne nhwiren ne kurinji a ɛfefɛw pɛnkoro wɔ mfe dumien mu. N’asɛmti ne punarthal, adɔfo no kokoam nhyiam. Ne nkurɔfo boaboa ɛwo ano, wwɛn atoko mfuw no fi akɔre ho na wɔbɔ abɔmmɔ wɔ kwae mu.
The murasu is the great drum of Sangam l: Murasu yɛ Sangam nhoma ahorow mu sanku kɛse, a wɔbɔ ma ahene, ma ɔko, ma baguam dawurubɔ ne guasodeyɛ ahorow — na ne nne no ankasa yɛ adehye tumidi ho sɛnkyerɛnne. Mpɔtam a wɔyɛ akuafo wɔ amanne kwan so no de nsubɔnten, abura, atare, nsuten, ne nsukorabea a wɔde gugu nnɔbae so dii dwuma de boaa kuayɛ. Abakɔsɛm mu nsu a wɔde gugu nnɔbae so a ɛho hia sen biara no mu biako ne Kallanai, anaa Grand Anicut, a ɛwɔ Kaveri Asubɔnten no agya no. Wɔ atetesɛm mu no, wɔkyerɛ sɛ Chola hene Karikala na ɔyɛe, na wɔyɛɛ no ​​sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ a wɔbɛhwɛ asubɔnten mu nsu so na wɔadan no foforo de agugu nnɔbae so. Tamilfo kuayɛ nsase nso yɛɛ nsukorabea ne nsukorabea ahorow a ɛboaboa osutɔ nsu a ɛba bere biara mu ano na wɔkyekyɛ. Saa nhyehyɛe ahorow yi boaa kuayɛ wɔ mmeae a osu nkutoo ntɔ no. Ná wɔn a wɔbɛhwɛ so no hwehwɛ sɛ mpɔtam hɔfo yɛ biako na wɔde asɛyɛde di nsu ho dwuma. Amanne kwan so nsu a wɔde gugu nnɔbae so da so ara yɛ asɛm a ɛho hia na ama yɛate abusuabɔ a ɛda kuayɛ, mfiridwuma, nnipa a wɔte hɔ, ne nneɛma a atwa yɛn ho ahyia a wɔsakra no ntam wɔ Tamil Nadu no ase.

When water could not flow naturally from: Sɛ nsu ntumi mfi asubɔnten, atare anaa abura mu nkɔ afuw mu wɔ abɔde mu a, na akuafo hia akwan a wɔbɛfa so ayɛn. Tamilfo kuayɛ mu amammerɛ mu nneyɛe no bi ne mfiri a wɔde nsa ma nsu so te sɛ bokiti, nketewa ne mfiri a wɔde lever di dwuma. Picottah a wɔtaa ka ho asɛm sɛ lever nhyehyɛe a ɛkari pɛ no ma obi tumi ma nsu so a ɔmmɔ mmɔden kɛse sen sɛ ɔde ne nsa bɛsoa. Lever mfiri a wɔtaa de di dwuma no de dua tenten bi a wɔde gyina pivot so na edi dwuma, a wɔde ade bi abata n’awiei biako na wɔde counterweight abata ano. Nea ɔyɛ adwuma no de ade no sian kɔ nsu no mu na ɔma so ma nsu da mpan kɔ nsu kwan anaa afuw bi mu. Tamil nhoma ahorow a Ahananuru, Maduraikanchi ne Silappadikaram ka ho no kura nsɛm a wɔakyerɛ ase sɛ ɛyɛ nneyɛe a wɔde ma nsu so ho adanse, na abakɔsɛm mu nkyerɛwee ahorow ka nsase a wɔde mfiri a ɛte sɛ picottah gugugu so ho asɛm.
